content.overview: Section 165 provides that no person shall hold office as a director, including any alternate directorship, in more than twenty companies at the same time, of which the maximum number of public companies shall not exceed ten. Members may by special resolution specify a lower number. A person who holds office in more than the permitted number must choose which offices to vacate within the specified period.
content.glance: Maximum 20 directorships (including alternate); of which public companies ≤10; members may set a lower cap by special resolution; excess must be vacated within the prescribed period.
content.study: No person, after the commencement of this Act, shall hold office as a director, including any alternate directorship, in more than twenty companies at the same time: provided that the maximum number of public companies in which a person can be appointed as a director shall not exceed ten. In reckoning the limit, dormant companies are excluded as the section provides. A private company that is a holding or subsidiary of a public company is treated as a public company for this count. The members of a company may, by special resolution, specify any lesser number of companies in which a director of the company may act as directors. A person holding office in more than the permitted number must choose the companies in which to continue and resign from the rest within the period specified. Current-law framing: count all directorships including alternate; separate public-company count; apply special-resolution lower cap if any; require vacation of excess.

sections.heading: Overall Cap
sections.body: No more than twenty companies at the same time, including alternate directorships.

sections.heading: Public-Company Cap
sections.body: Of the twenty, public companies shall not exceed ten. A private company that is a holding or subsidiary of a public company counts as a public company for this purpose.

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.body: Dormant companies are excluded from the count as the section provides.

sections.heading: Lower Cap by Members
sections.body: Members may by special resolution specify a lesser number for directors of that company.

sections.heading: Excess
sections.body: A person exceeding the limit must choose which offices to retain and vacate the rest within the specified period.

examples.title: Public-company limit
examples.body: A person is a director of twelve public companies. Section 165 is breached on the public-company cap of ten, even if the overall count is under twenty.

examples.title: Holding/subsidiary private company
examples.body: A private company that is a subsidiary of a public company counts as a public company toward the ten-public-company limit under s. 165.

hypotheticals.question: Do alternate directorships count toward the twenty-company limit?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 165 expressly includes any alternate directorship in the count.

distinctions.title: Number of directorships (s. 165) vs board composition (s. 149)
distinctions.left: Cap on how many companies one person may serve as director
distinctions.right: Minimum and maximum number of directors on a single company’s board

misconceptions.trap: Only public-company directorships are capped; private companies are unlimited.
misconceptions.correction: There is an overall cap of twenty companies (including private) and a separate public-company cap of ten.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 165 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Count all directorships including alternate. II. Count public companies (including private holding/subsidiary of public). III. Apply any special-resolution lower cap. IV. Require vacation of excess. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: List of directorships; public vs private count; special resolution if any; precise relief.

examTips: Private subsidiary of public counts as public.
Members may set a lower cap.
